mainTopic: Farm and water work on חול המועד and in שביעית: thinning and watering vegetables, ditches around vines, digging and repairing water channels, and clearing public rivers
overview: This amud works through several lines of the משנה about farm work on חול המועד. First, the word מדלין is explained as thinning out vegetables. רבינא then shows a ברייתא where it clearly means drawing water, and that explanation is dropped. Next, עוגיות are explained as round ditches around vines: new ones may not be dug, but old ones may be cleared. The גמרא then asks why רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids digging a new water channel in שביעית. Two reasons are given, 'it looks like hoeing' and 'it readies the banks for planting', and the גמרא works out where they differ. אמימר's version of the משנה raises a contradiction from a manure pit, which is answered in two ways. The גמרא defines a 'damaged' channel that may be repaired, measuring it in handbreadths, and ends that discussion with a תיקו. Finally, three rulings allow towns to clear their rivers, because a river the public drinks from counts as a public need.

steps.title: Explaining the word מדלין as pulling out
steps.stepSummary: The word מדלין in the ברייתא is explained to mean 'pulling out', meaning thinning out vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: "מדלין" means pulling out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines a hard word, מדלין, from a ברייתא it has been discussing. The explanation is that it means pulling out some of the vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדלין could mean drawing water or thinning out plants. This explanation picks 'thinning out', so the ברייתא would be talking about pulling out crowded vegetables on חול המועד in order to eat them. This reading will be challenged in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: A word that can mean 'draw (water)' or 'thin out'
The intermediate days of a יום טוב

phrases.english: "Madlin" means pulling out.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מַדְלִין״ — שַׁלּוֹפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by defining a term from the ongoing discussion.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה that the root means thinning out
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about thinning vines shows that the word מידל is used for thinning, not only for drawing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who thins out vines may thin out the poor's vines just as he thins out his own. That is רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר says he may thin out his own vines but not the poor's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the word מידל can mean 'thinning out.' The משנה uses this word for thinning grapevines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real point is not the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר about the poor's vines. The point is the word itself: the משנה uses מידל for pulling out extra growth from vines, so it is reasonable to read מדלין the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The poor (here, the part of the vineyard left for them)

phrases.english: As we learned: one who thins out the vines,
phrases.notes: This משנה is from מסכת פאה.

phrases.english: just as he thins out his own,
so too he may thin out those of the poor,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Meir says: with his own he is permitted,
but he is not permitted with those of the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that מדלין means thinning out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פאה, which uses מידל for thinning vines.

steps.title: A ברייתא where מדלין clearly means drawing water
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the definition with a ברייתא that says 'מדלין water for vegetables.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But it was taught in a ברייתא: One may draw water for vegetables in order to eat them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבה תוספאה's definition. He quotes a ברייתא that says outright that מדלין is done with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'מדלין מים', drawing water, to vegetables so they can be eaten. That matches the ברייתא being discussed word for word, and here the word plainly means irrigating, not pulling out. So the 'thinning' explanation seems wrong.

phrases.english: He said to him: But it was taught:
phrases.notes: רבינא is the one speaking, and he is talking to רבה תוספאה, who gave the 'pulling out' explanation.

phrases.english: One may draw water for vegetables in order to eat them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that מדלין means pulling out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says 'מדלין water', so the word must mean drawing water in this context.

steps.title: He accepts the challenge and takes back his explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבה תוספאה answers: if a ברייתא teaches it, then that is how it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it was taught, it was taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה תוספאה does not argue. He admits that if a ברייתא says this, he takes back his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explanation by an אמורא cannot stand against a clear ברייתא. So מדלין in our ברייתא means drawing water to vegetables, and the 'pulling out' reading is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was taught, it was taught. In other words, I take back what I said.

steps.whatToRemember: מדלין in the ברייתא means drawing water to vegetables so they can be eaten. The explanation 'pulling out' was taken back because of an explicit ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אי תניא תניא' is not an answer that defends the first view. It means the speaker gives up and accepts the ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it was taught, it was taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי תַּנְיָא — תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives in to the challenge in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is accepted, and מדלין means drawing water, not thinning out.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: no עוגיות for vines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה: one may not make עוגיות for vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not make עוגיות for the vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. This quote sets up the next step, which asks what the word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה forbids making עוגיות for vines on חול המועד. The word is unclear, so the גמרא brings it up in order to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: Round ditches dug around the base of trees

phrases.english: And one may not make ugiyyot for the vines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין עוּגִיּוֹת לַגְּפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד one may not make עוגיות for vines.

steps.title: What are עוגיות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word עוגיות means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are עוגיות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the meaning of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. The גמרא just wants to know which activity the משנה is forbidding.

phrases.english: What are ugiyyot?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי עוּגִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word quoted in step 5 means.

steps.title: רב יהודה: they are בנכי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that עוגיות are what people call בנכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: They are בנכי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by giving the everyday Aramaic word for עוגיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בנכי are round ditches dug around the base of a vine. They hold water for the roots. So the משנה forbids digging these ditches on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Round ditches around the base of a vine (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Binkei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בַּנְכֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עוגיות are בנכי, round ditches around vines.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the definition
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says that עוגיות are ditches around the base of olive trees and vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: These are עוגיות: ditches at the base of olive trees and at the base of vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב יהודה's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls עוגיות בדידין, ditches at the roots of olive trees and vines. That matches רב יהודה's בנכי, so his explanation is confirmed by an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: Ditches or hollows dug in the ground

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
These are ugiyyot:
ditches that are at the bases of olive trees
and that are at the bases of vines.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's definition of עוגיות as round ditches.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא defining עוגיות as בדידין at the base of olive trees and vines.

steps.title: But רב יהודה allowed a family to make such ditches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב יהודה himself allowed the family of בר ציתאי to make בנכי for their vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יהודה allowed the family of בר ציתאי to make בנכי for their vineyards!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that these ditches are forbidden. It points to a case where רב יהודה allowed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה just said that עוגיות, which the משנה forbids, are בנכי. Yet he allowed a family to make בנכי, apparently on חול המועד. His ruling seems to go against the משנה and against his own definition.

phrases.english: Is that so? But Rav Yehuda permitted
the family of bar Tzitai
to make binkei for their vineyards!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב יְהוּדָה שְׁרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from the משנה as explained in steps 5-7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not make עוגיות (בנכי) on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה's own ruling allowed making בנכי, which seems to contradict the משנה he explained.

steps.title: New ditches are forbidden, old ones are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה forbids digging new ditches, and רב יהודה allowed fixing up old ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about new ones, that one is about old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources deal with different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging a brand-new ditch is real work, so the משנה forbids it. Clearing out an old ditch that is already there is a smaller job, and that is what רב יהודה allowed. Both are בנכי, but they get different rulings on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This introduces a resolution.

steps.whatToRemember: עוגיות are round ditches around the base of trees. On חול המועד one may not dig new ones, but one may clear out old ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in הלכות חול המועד: starting new work is treated more strictly than keeping up something that already exists.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is about new ones,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה, which forbids making עוגיות.

phrases.english: that is about old ones.
phrases.notes: 'That' is רב יהודה's ruling. The old ditches only need to be cleared out.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּחַדְתֵי, הָא בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): new ditches compared with old ditches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the משנה and רב יהודה's ruling were about the same activity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה forbids digging new ditches, and רב יהודה permitted clearing old ones.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids making a water channel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says one may not make a water channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: One may not make a water channel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This quote sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is talking about both חול המועד and שביעית. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids digging a new channel to bring water to the fields during both times.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel dug to bring water to fields

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may not make the water channel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of עוגיות to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not make a new water channel on חול המועד or in שביעית.

steps.title: Why is it forbidden in שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: The reason for חול המועד is clear, since it is hard work. But why is it forbidden in שביעית?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for חול המועד, because he is working hard. But what is the reason for שביעית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reason for חול המועד and asks why digging a channel would be forbidden in שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד, hard work is the problem. In שביעית the problem is working the land so plants grow, and digging a channel does not seem to be that kind of work. So the גמרא needs a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
He puts in effort, works hard
The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden

phrases.english: It makes sense for the festival days:
because he is working hard,
but in the seventh year, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מוֹעֵד מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא טָרַח, אֶלָּא שְׁבִיעִית מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason digging a water channel is forbidden in שביעית.

steps.title: Two reasons: it looks like hoeing, or it readies the banks for planting
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי אבא בר ממל disagree. One says it looks like hoeing. The other says the dug-up dirt readies the channel's banks for planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי אבא בר ממל argue about this. One says: because it looks like he is hoeing. The other says: because he prepares its banks for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers from two אמוראים to explain the שביעית problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about how it looks: people watching might think he is hoeing his field. The second reason is about a real result: the fresh dirt he piles on the sides becomes ready for planting.

keyTerms.meaning: Looks like he is hoeing the field

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגוּ בַּהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Abba bar Memel argued about this.
One said: because it looks like he is hoeing.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּכְשִׁיר אֲגַפֶּיהָ לִזְרִיעָה.
phrases.english: And the other said: because he prepares its banks for planting.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגוּ בַּהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either because it looks like hoeing, or because it prepares the banks for planting.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would give different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case where the two reasons would lead to different rulings. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons forbid a normal channel. The גמרא wants a situation where one reason applies and the other does not, so we can see why the argument matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the two opinions by asking for their practical difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different rulings.

steps.title: First suggestion: when water flows in right away
steps.stepSummary: The difference is when water flows into the channel right after he digs. Then it is still forbidden by the 'banks' reason, but not by the 'looks like hoeing' reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when water comes in right after him. According to the one who says it readies the banks for planting, it is forbidden. According to the one who says it looks like hoeing, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a case: water flows into the channel right away. It shows that the two reasons rule differently here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If water comes in at once, everyone sees it is a channel, so it no longer looks like hoeing. But the dirt is still piled on the banks, so the 'banks' reason still forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּקָא אָתוּ מַיָּא בָּתְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: There is a difference between them when the water comes right after him.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּכְשִׁיר אֲגַפֶּיהָ לִזְרִיעָה — אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: The one who said 'because he prepares its banks for planting': there is a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹדֵר — לֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: and the one who said 'because it looks like hoeing': there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּקָא אָתוּ מַיָּא בָּתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 with a first suggested case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When water flows in right away, only the 'banks' reason forbids it.

steps.title: But the 'hoeing' opinion should worry about the banks too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion: why would the 'looks like hoeing' opinion ignore the real problem of readying the banks for planting?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the one who says 'because it looks like hoeing' should also be worried that he prepares its banks for planting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 15. It argues that the 'hoeing' opinion should also forbid this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Readying the banks for planting is a real result, not just how things look. No one would allow it. So even the 'hoeing' opinion should forbid the case where water flows in, and that means there is no difference there.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said

phrases.english: But according to the one who said 'because it looks like hoeing,'
let him also worry that he prepares its banks for planting!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹדֵר, לֵיחוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical difference proposed in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'hoeing' opinion permits the case where water flows in right away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Readying the banks for planting is a real problem that every opinion should accept, so the 'hoeing' opinion should also forbid that case.

steps.title: Real difference: when he throws the dirt far away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new case: he takes the dirt and throws it far outside. Then the banks are not readied, but it still looks like hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference is when he takes the dirt out and throws it far outside. According to the one who says it readies the banks for planting, it is allowed. According to the one who says it looks like hoeing, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first suggestion and offers a different case where the two reasons really rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dirt is thrown far away, nothing is piled on the banks, so the 'banks' reason has no problem. But the digging still looks like hoeing, so the 'hoeing' reason still forbids it. Here the difference works the opposite way from step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes from it (the dirt from the channel)

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons forbid digging a new channel in שביעית: 'it looks like hoeing' and 'it readies the banks for planting.' They differ when the dirt is thrown far away. Then only the 'hoeing' reason forbids it.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch: in the first suggestion the 'banks' opinion was the stricter one. In the final answer the 'hoeing' opinion is the stricter one.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them
when he takes the dirt from it and throws it outside.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּכְשִׁיר אֲגַפֶּיהָ לִזְרִיעָה — לֵיכָּא.
phrases.english: According to the one who said 'because he prepares its banks for planting': there is no prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹדֵר — אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: According to the one who said 'because it looks like hoeing': there is a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ וְשָׁדֵי לְבָרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by replacing the first suggestion with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the suggested practical difference with a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was thought to be when water flows in right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is when the dirt is thrown far away. Then only the 'hoeing' opinion forbids it.

steps.title: Why doesn't the 'banks' opinion worry about hoeing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the opinion that the problem is readying the banks for planting. Why doesn't that opinion also worry that the digging looks like hoeing?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who said the reason is that he readies the banks for planting, let him also worry that it looks like hoeing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the reverse of step 16. It wants to know why the 'banks' opinion ignores the 'looks like hoeing' concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the גמרא asked why the 'hoeing' opinion ignores the banks problem. Now it asks the opposite about the case from step 17, where he throws the dirt far away. Even there the digging could look like hoeing, so why does the 'banks' opinion allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said
Its banks (the sides of the channel)

phrases.english: And according to the one who said
because he readies its banks for planting,
let him be concerned because it looks like hoeing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּכְשִׁיר אֲגַפֶּיהָ לִזְרִיעָה, לֵיחוּשׁ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the challenge of step 16, now aimed at the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'readying the banks' opinion from step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even when the dirt is thrown far away, the digging could still look like hoeing, so that opinion should forbid that case too.

steps.title: A real hoer puts the dirt back in place
steps.stepSummary: Hoeing does not look like digging a channel, because a hoer puts the dirt right back where it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hoer, too, when he lifts up dirt, puts it back down in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. When the dirt is thrown far away, the digging does not look like hoeing, so the 'banks' opinion has no reason to forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who hoes loosens the dirt and leaves it in the same spot. Here the digger throws the dirt far away, so anyone watching can see he is not hoeing. That is why the 'banks' opinion allows this case, while the 'hoeing' opinion still forbids it (step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: One who hoes or loosens soil

phrases.english: A hoer, too,
when he lifts up dirt,
puts it down in its place.
phrases.notes: So when someone moves the dirt away from the spot, it is clear he isn't hoeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹדֵר נָמֵי, כִּי קָא שָׁקֵיל, בְּדוּכְתֵּיהּ מַנַּח לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the two actions do not look alike.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even when the dirt is thrown far away, the digging looks like hoeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hoer leaves the dirt in place. When the digger throws the dirt far away, it does not look like hoeing, so the 'banks' opinion allows that case.

steps.title: אמימר's version: the reason is 'looks like hoeing'
steps.stepSummary: אמימר taught the משנה with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reason stated outright: it looks like hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר would teach it as 'because it looks like hoeing.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. אמימר had a version of the משנה that gives 'looks like hoeing' as the reason, and this sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, two אמוראים argued about what the reason was. In אמימר's version the משנה itself says the reason is 'looks like hoeing'.

phrases.english: אמימר would teach it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the משנה about digging a new water channel.

phrases.english: as 'because it looks like hoeing,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר מַתְנֵי לַהּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּעוֹדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the two-reason discussion and brings a version where the משנה states the reason outright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids digging a new channel in שביעית because it looks like hoeing.

steps.title: Does רבי אלעזר בן עזריה really forbid whatever looks like hoeing?
steps.stepSummary: אמימר had a problem: this ruling of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה seems to clash with another ruling of his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he found one statement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה hard to square with another statement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: Did רבי אלעזר בן עזריה really say that anything that looks like hoeing is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces a contradiction between two rulings of the same תנא. The other ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on אמימר's version, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids anything that looks like hoeing. The גמרא asks whether he really holds that as a general rule, because elsewhere he seems not to.

phrases.english: and it was difficult for him
one statement of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
against another of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: But did Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya say
that anything that looks like hoeing is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אַדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אמימר's version to raise a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids anything that looks like hoeing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling of his (brought next) allows digging that could look like hoeing.

steps.title: The contradiction: digging a pit for manure is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about piling manure in שביעית shows that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה lets a person dig a pit three handbreadths deep, even though digging could look like hoeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And contrast it with this: A person may make his manure into a storage pile. רבי מאיר forbids it unless he digs three handbreadths deep or raises it three handbreadths high. If he had a small amount there already, he may keep adding to it. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids it unless he digs three deep, or raises it three high, or puts it on a rock!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second ruling that clashes with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's channel ruling. In the manure case he lets a person dig a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The manure pile has to be set apart so it does not look like he is fertilizing the field. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows doing this by digging a pit three handbreadths deep. Digging in a field could look like hoeing, so he must not forbid everything that looks like hoeing.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it (here is a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get stuck on the argument between רבי מאיר and the first opinion. The only point that matters here is that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows digging a pit.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אמימר, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids digging a channel because it looks like hoeing. Yet he allows digging a pit for manure, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

phrases.english: And contrast it with this:
A person may make his manure into a storage pile.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה about שביעית. It is talking about piling manure in his field.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir forbids it,
unless he digs it three handbreadths deep,
or raises it three handbreadths high.
If he had a small amount there already,
he may keep adding to it.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya forbids it
unless he digs three deep,
or raises it three high,
or puts it on a rock!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם אֶת זִבְלוֹ אוֹצָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the contradicting source that step 21 announced.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reason 'looks like hoeing' for the water channel (אמימר's version).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the manure case he allows digging a three-handbreadth pit, which could look like hoeing. So 'looks like hoeing' cannot be a general reason for him to forbid something.

steps.title: Two answers for the manure-pit case
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי אבא בר ממל each explain why digging a manure pit in שביעית does not look like hoeing. One says the pit was already dug deep before. The other says the pile of manure shows what he is doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי אבא בר ממל answered. One said: the case is where he had already deepened the pit. The other said: his manure proves what he is doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22: how can רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allow digging a pit in שביעית if digging can look like hoeing? Two אמוראים give two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one changes the case: the pit was dug earlier, so no new digging is happening that could look like hoeing. Answer two keeps the case but says onlookers can see the manure pile, so they understand he is making a pit for manure and not working the field. Digging a new water channel in שביעית has no such clear sign, so the worry about hoeing stays there.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them said (used when two scholars each give a view and we are not told who said which)
Proves about him (shows everyone what he is doing)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Abba bar Memel [answered]:
One said: for example, where he had already deepened it,
And one said: his manure proves [what he is doing].

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱמִיק, וְחַד אָמַר: זִיבְלוֹ מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 21-22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two answers: one narrows the case (the pit was already dug), and one points to a clear sign (the manure) that shows what he is doing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Digging a pit in שביעית should be forbidden because it looks like hoeing, just like digging a new water channel in שביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The manure-pit case is different: either there is no new digging, or the manure shows his purpose, so it does not look like hoeing.

steps.title: What counts as a 'damaged' channel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים's ruling that a damaged channel may be repaired on חול המועד, and asks what 'damaged' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may repair a damaged channel during the Festival.' What is meant by 'damaged'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks what the word 'damaged' means. This sets up רבי אבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allow repairing a damaged channel but not digging a new one. To know where the line is, we need to know exactly how damaged the channel must be.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.english: And one may repair the damaged [channel] during the Festival.
What is "damaged"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְקוּלְקֶלֶת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of a 'damaged' channel that may be repaired on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי אבא: from one handbreadth back to six
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that a channel that silted up to only one handbreadth deep may be dug back out to six handbreadths.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: if it became only one handbreadth deep, he may restore it to six handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question with a concrete example of a 'damaged' channel and how far it may be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The channel used to be six handbreadths deep, but mud filled it until only one handbreadth was left. Clearing it back to its normal depth counts as repairing, not making something new. This gives a measuring point the גמרא will use next.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it (brings it back to)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
That if it was [only] a handbreadth deep,
he sets it at six handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה עֲמוּקָּה טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A damaged channel is one that silted up to one handbreadth. It may be dug back out to six handbreadths.

steps.title: The obvious cases: too shallow and too much work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says two cases are obvious. Half a handbreadth to three is forbidden because such a shallow channel is useless. Two to twelve is forbidden because it is too much work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: half a handbreadth to three is nothing, since water does not flow well in it. Two to twelve is not allowed, since it takes extra effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבי אבא's rule on other measurements and says some answers are obvious. This sets up the harder question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases keep the same proportion as רבי אבא's case (1 to 6), yet both are forbidden. A three-handbreadth channel does not carry enough water, so the work gives no real benefit. Twelve handbreadths means far too much digging. So the rule is not just about the proportion.

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא, חֲצִי טֶפַח עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: It is obvious: half a handbreadth [deepened] to three handbreadths,
since water does not flow [properly through it],
it is nothing.
Two handbreadths [deepened] to twelve,
since he goes to extra effort,
no [it is not allowed].

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, חֲצִי טֶפַח עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אבא's measurement by testing other cases with the same proportion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping the 1-to-6 proportion is not enough: a channel too shallow to be useful, or digging that takes too much work, is forbidden.

steps.title: What about two handbreadths to seven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about deepening a channel from two to seven handbreadths. It is five handbreadths of digging like רבי אבא's case, but the digging goes one handbreadth deeper.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about two to seven? Here he digs five handbreadths, and there he digs five. Or perhaps, since there is an extra handbreadth of depth, it is more effort?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a case in between and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: in both cases he digs exactly five handbreadths, so this should be allowed. Side two: the channel ends up one handbreadth deeper than six, and digging lower down is harder, so maybe it counts as extra effort.

phrases.english: Two handbreadths [deepened] to seven, what is [the law]?
Here he deepens five,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רבי אבא's case: from one handbreadth to six.

phrases.english: and here he deepens five,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא טֶפַח יַתִּירָא
phrases.english: or perhaps: since there is an extra handbreadth,
there is more effort?

steps.triggerLanguage: טִפְחַיִים עַל שִׁבְעָה מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious cases to a harder case in between.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the limit depend on how much he digs (five handbreadths) or on how deep the channel ends up (more than six)?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the two-to-seven question unanswered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion without deciding the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the extra handbreadth of depth makes the job forbidden. So the case of two to seven handbreadths remains an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question stays unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא allows clearing a channel from one handbreadth back to six. A channel too shallow to be useful (three) or digging that takes too much work (two to twelve) is forbidden. Two to seven stays an open question: תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of Step 27 without answering it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a channel may be deepened from two handbreadths to seven on חול המועד stays undecided.

steps.title: אביי allows clearing a river
steps.stepSummary: אביי permitted the people of בר המדך to clear out their river on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי allowed the people of בר המדך to clear out the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from theory to real life and reports a practical ruling by אביי. He let a town clear out its river on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with fixing small water channels. This story shows that a whole river serving a town may also be cleaned on חול המועד. It is the first of three similar stories.

keyTerms.meaning: to clear out, to sweep away what is blocking

phrases.english: Abaye permitted the people of Bar Hamdakh
phrases.notes: בר המדך is the name of a town. בני means 'the people of' here, not 'sons of'.

phrases.english: to clear out the river.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי שְׁרָא לִבְנֵי בַּר הַמְדָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו, the גמרא turns to practical rulings about clearing waterways on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearing a town's river is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה allows dredging a blocked river
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה permitted the people of סכותא to dig out a river that had become blocked up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה allowed the people of סכותא to dig out a river that had become blocked.
steps.whatsHappening: A second practical story: רבי ירמיה let a town dig out a river that had filled up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes a step further than אביי's case. Here the river was actually stopped up, so real digging was needed, and it was still permitted.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה שְׁרָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי סָכוּתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya permitted the people of Sekhavta
to dig out a river that had become blocked.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה שְׁרָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי סָכוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story in the same series, with a blocked river instead of a cluttered one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging out a blocked town river is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: רב אשי allows cleaning out the בורניץ River
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי permitted the people of his town, מתא מחסיא, to clean out the בורניץ River.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי allowed the people of מתא מחסיא to clean out the בורניץ River.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story: רב אשי let his own town clean out their local river on חול המועד. Right after this he will explain his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third ruling in a row that allows river work on חול המועד. Unlike the first two, this one comes with a stated reason, given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: to clean out, to clear a river so the water flows

phrases.english: Rav Ashi permitted them,
the people of Mata Meḥasya,
to clean out the Burnitz River.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי שְׁרָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third story in the series. This one leads into an explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleaning out the town's river is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: Why it is allowed: a public drinking source is a public need
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that since the public drinks from the river, cleaning it counts as a public need, and the משנה allows all public needs on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Since the public drinks from it, it is like a public need. And we learned in the משנה: one may take care of all public needs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the reason for his ruling. He proves it from the משנה's rule that public needs may be taken care of on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that the river is not one person's private project. Many people drink from it, so it falls under צרכי רבים. The משנה already said all public needs are allowed, so the work is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Work on a waterway that many people drink from counts as a public need, and the משנה allows all public needs on חול המועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the general rule behind all three stories. River work is allowed because it serves the public, not just because it is water work.

phrases.english: He said: Since the public drinks from it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב אשי, explaining his own ruling.

phrases.english: it is considered like a public need,
and we learned: One may tend to all public needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁתוּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּים כְּרַבִּים דָּמֵי, וּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning and source for רב אשי's ruling in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's permission to clean out the בורניץ River on חול המועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: עושין כל צורכי רבים, one may tend to all public needs on חול המועד

steps.title: Starting the next quote from the משנה: 'one may repair'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the next phrase of the משנה, 'and one may repair...', to open a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may repair...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא starts quoting the next words of the משנה, and the discussion of them continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The river discussion is finished, and the גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה. Only the first words appear here, so the full quote and its discussion come next.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full statement. It is just the opening words of the next משנה quote, so do not look for a ruling here.

phrases.english: And one may repair

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the river stories and starts a new section on the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening quote of the משנה: during חול המועד one may repair certain things. The rest of the quote follows.
